source: The channel's opening statement (posted before episode 1 and pinned). Not a story episode: it says what the series is. Facts: the Mahabharata's traditional count is about 100,000 verses (the epic calls itself the 'shatasahasri samhita', the collection of a hundred thousand); the Critical Edition (Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune, 1919–1966) constitutes a text of nearly 75,000 verses. The frame story (Sauti at Naimisha, retelling what Vaishampayana recited at Janamejaya's sacrifice) opens the Adi Parva. Every frame and every sound of the series is generated by code; the voices are Kokoro-82M text-to-speech.
structure: COLD OPEN (the hook over Sauti's fire at Naimisha, big text from frame 1) → the series title (hook post) → the statement in ten short shots (three new title moments: the hundred thousand verses, the Critical Edition, 'made in code') → 'It begins with a storyteller' → a silent Next card for episode 1 that dissolves back into frame 1.

strings.ceSource: Our text: the BORI Critical Edition
strings.sourceNote: Southern manuscripts and the Puranas · not in the Critical Edition

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json. The narrator (am_michael) carries the statement; Sauti (bm_fable) opens it and closes it, at his fire.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: What does the Mahabharata actually say?
lines.say: What does the Mahabharata [p:60] actually say?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (moving from frame 1): night at Naimisha, Sauti speaking at the fire, the sages listening, sparks rising; the question in big text from frame 1; the series title in the post.

lines.text: It is often called the longest poem ever composed: about a hundred thousand verses, by the traditional count.
lines.say: It is often called the longest poem ever composed: [p:120] about a hundred thousand verses, [p:60] by the traditional count.
lines.note: TITLE MOMENT 1: palm-leaf pages fly in and stack into a towering pile in the dark; a gold counter rolls up to 100,000 (beats[1]→beats[2]).

lines.text: Nearly seventy-five thousand, in the Critical Edition.
lines.say: Nearly seventy-five thousand, [p:60] in the Critical Edition.
lines.note: The counter settles; a second figure (≈ 75,000) rises under it, labelled 'in the Critical Edition'; the pile is trimmed (the later additions drift away as faint leaves).

lines.text: Most of us know it through retellings, and through television.
lines.say: Most of us know it through retellings, [p:80] and through television.
lines.note: Three sepia memory niches fan in (a grandmother's lamp, a painted scene, the glow of a screen): the epic as it is remembered.

lines.text: This series tells it the way Vyasa's text tells it.
lines.say: This series tells it [p:60] the way Vyasa's text tells it.
lines.note: Vyasa at his hermitage in the morning light, the verses rising from him as gold script (episode 4's image).

lines.text: We follow the Critical Edition. And where a beloved tale comes from later tradition, we say so.
lines.say: We follow the Critical Edition. [p:250] And where a beloved tale comes from later tradition, [p:80] we say so.
lines.note: TITLE MOMENT 2: a manuscript unrolls with the edition's name on a lacquer plaque; on 'beloved tale' (beats[1]) cut to Shiva with the blue throat, 'As tradition tells it' on screen, with the source line (episode 14's honest tag).

lines.text: One minute at a time, episode by episode, in order, from the very first frame story.
lines.say: One minute at a time, [p:80] episode by episode, [p:80] in order, [p:60] from the very first frame story.
lines.note: Quick cuts on the beats through four released episodes, each with a small badge: the storyteller at the fire (ep 1), the snake sacrifice (ep 8), the churning (ep 12), Garuda (ep 19).

lines.text: It is drawn like the old temple murals, and every frame is made in code.
lines.say: It is drawn like the old temple murals, [p:100] and every frame is made in code.
lines.note: TITLE MOMENT 3: lines of the series' own drawing code scroll on the left; a wipe paints Garuda over them (beats[1]→beats[2]).

lines.text: The voices are synthetic: a text-to-speech model, not actors.
lines.say: The voices are synthetic: [p:100] a text-to-speech model, [p:60] not actors.
lines.note: Sauti close at the fire, a gold waveform under his words; the plaque names the model (Kokoro-82M).

lines.text: No hype, nothing twisted: the essence of the epic, condensed, as it is told.
lines.say: No hype, [p:80] nothing twisted: [p:150] the essence of the epic, [p:60] condensed, [p:60] as it is told.
lines.note: The field of the eighteen days at dusk, the two hosts' banners along the horizon, dust rising: the war the whole epic leads to, held quiet.

lines.text: If you walk with us, longer episodes will follow, and go deeper.
lines.say: If you walk with us, [p:100] longer episodes will follow, [p:80] and go deeper.
lines.note: Dawn over the sea: Garuda flies on toward the rising light, small and then larger (the long road ahead).

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It begins with a storyteller, arriving at a fire in the forest.
lines.say: It begins with a storyteller, [p:100] arriving at a fire in the forest.
lines.note: Dawn in the Naimisha forest: the lone storyteller with his staff walks toward the far smoke of the sages' fire.
The silent card: BEGIN · the niche opens on Sauti at the fire · 'Episode 1 · The Storyteller Arrives' under the series title; then the loop back to frame 1.
